title: The Simple Pendulum: Why Mass Doesn't Matter
topic: Simple pendulum — for small swings, T = 2π√(L/g); the period depends on length and gravity, not mass

beats.narration: A weight on a string — pull it sideways and let go. What sets the rhythm of its swing?

elements.content: Manimo bobs in centre-screen
Pull a weight on a string — what sets the rhythm?

beats.narration: Hang a mass from a string of length L. Pull it to angle theta. Gravity pulls straight down, but only the tangential component, minus m g sine theta, restores it toward vertical.

elements.content: Pivot bracket at top — small horizontal bar with hatching
Vertical dashed reference line from pivot straight down (rest position)
String from pivot to bob at angle θ to the right
Small arc between vertical and string near pivot, with θ label
L label centred along the string (italic serif)
Bob — filled amber circle at end of string
m label right of bob
Gravity vector straight down from bob (rose, length 70)
mg label below gravity arrow tip
Tangential restoring force arrow perpendicular to string, pointing back toward vertical
−mg sin θ label near tangential arrow
only the tangential component restores it

beats.narration: For small swings, sine theta is approximately theta. The equation of motion becomes the second derivative of theta plus g over L theta equals zero — exactly the spring equation, with omega zero equal to the square root of g over L.

elements.content: sin θ ≈ θ
small-angle approximation
d²θ/dt² + (g/L) θ = 0
same shape as the spring equation
ω₀ = √(g/L)

beats.narration: The period is two pi over omega zero — so T equals two pi times the square root of L over g. Notice what is missing: the mass.

elements.content: period of one full swing
T = 2π√(L/g)
longer string
L ↑  →  T ↑
stronger gravity
g ↑  →  T ↓

beats.narration: Heavier bob, lighter bob — same length swings to the same beat. Gravity sets the metronome.

elements.content: Heavier bob, lighter bob — same length, same beat.
(no m in the formula — gravity sets the metronome)
